newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks open lower, gold stocks fall again.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks open lower, gold stocks fall again.

text.p: Australian shares opened lower on Tuesday with gold stocks still in near free-fall and the broader market tracking U.S. declines triggered by profit-taking.

"The resource sector is not exactly supporting, and a weaker night on Wall Street gave us the lead. Until the gold situation rectifies itself, the selling may continue," one Brisbane-based dealer said.
At 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), the All Ordinaries index had lost 20.2 points to 2,692.8.

Gold stocks kept falling as gold bullion prices hit a fresh 12-year low of U$313.19 before bouncing in New York to U$318 an ounce. The sector index fell five percent in early trade and has plummeted around 15 percent since Thursday.
Dealers said a quick recovery for the sector was unlikely after the plunge since last week's news that the Reserve Bank of Australia has sold two thirds of its gold reserves.
Sector heavyweight Normandy Mining fell nine cents to A$1.23, its lowest level in four and a half years.
Newcrest Mining lost another 23 cents to A$2.79 and Lihir Gold 15 to A$1.79. Resolute Samantha dipped 26 cents to A$1.65.
Blue-chip diversified resource groups Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and WMC each shed 23 cents to A$19.02 and A$7.91 respectively.
"Almost all the big institutional stocks have come under pressure today," one dealer said.

Declines sharply outnumbered advances, although some sectors held up better than others. In the media sector, News Corp was steady at A$6.51 while Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd came down two cents to A$7.90.
